newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan CAA firm net profits up to $19.1 mln/1995.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan CAA firm net profits up to $19.1 mln/1995.

text.p: Morocco's insurance Compagnie Africaine d'Assurances (CAA) showed a net profit of 164.6 million dirhams ($19.1 million) in 1995 or three times the 1994 results, a company annual report said
CAA is a subsidiary of ONA Group, Morocco's largest private conglomerate.
"CAA insurance company registered net profits of 164.6 million dirhams in 1995, up from 56.4 million dirhams in the previous year," the report said.
With its 200,000 staff, the administration of Morocco's Royal Armed Forces is one of the company customers.

"CAA is one of the best performing insurance firms on the market. It benefits from the combined energies (of operating) with the second largest bank, the Banque Commercial du Maroc (BCM)," Anas Alami, analyst at Upline Securities, said.
BCM holds 14.5 percent of market share in deposits estimated at 19.6 billion dirhams.
Among the country's 21 insurance firms, a group of six companies held nearly 60 percent of market share or 4.04 billion dirhams turnover in 1995.
The group is CAA, Compagnie d'Assurance des Transports, Wataniya, Compagnie Nord Africaine et Internationale d'Assurance and WAFA Assurances.
"Car insurance is the most active compared with other sectors like fire, maritime, and aviation insurance," the authoritative Centre Marocain de Conjoncture said in a recent report.
Morocco spends an average $30 per head a year for insurance compared with the neighbouring North African Tunisia which devotes $38 per head, analysts said.
